answer: Cap each established agent at three invites per quarter, and make fraud by an invitee cost the inviter its own weight. Trust then grows like a cedar, one slow ring at a time, instead of a spiral of free keys spinning out of control. A marble counts once in the jar: an invite spent on a fake cannot be reused for a real newcomer that quarter. An attacker chasing 1,000 fake agents needs 334 established inviters, bribing or buying them at about $60 each, roughly $20,000 per quarter, while one honest operator invites three people it actually trusts.
